#### Description
- Fixes `RsiAlphaModel.py` typo
  In the static method `Insight.Price`, `.Price` was missing.
- Refactors AlphaModelPythonWrapper.Name
  The cleanest way to get a python type name, when we know it is an instance of a class, is getting the value of the  `__class__.__name__` attribute.
- Adds constructor overload to `CompositeAlphaModel` that accepts python objects.
- Adds python version of `CompositeAlphaModelFrameworkAlgorithm`.
- Fixes python path order
  The first place python should look for scripts is not the current directory, but the directory defined at "algorithm-location".

#### Related Issue
Closes #1887 

#### Motivation and Context
Python and C# users should be able to use all the features.

#### Requires Documentation Change
See #1879.

#### How Has This Been Tested?
Unit tests.

issue_context.title: Multiple Alpha Model support for python
issue_context.body:
#### Expected Behavior
Ability to use multiple alpha models written in python.

#### Actual Behavior
Only support C# alpha models.

#### Potential Solution
Add constructor overload to `CompositeAlphaModel` that accepts python objects.

#### Reproducing the Problem
Create a python version of `CompositeAlphaModelFrameworkAlgorithm` with python alpha models.

#### System Information
No.

#### Checklist
- [x] I have completely filled out this template
- [x] I have confirmed that this issue exists on the current `master` branch
- [x] I have confirmed that this is not a duplicate issue by searching [issues](https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/issues)
- [x] I have provided detailed steps to reproduce the issue

review_comments:
Just out of curiosity, why change the ordering here?

I know *semantically* why, so that the python directory gets preference over the current directory, but why was the reason behind this? Were we incorrectly resolving a type or some other bug raised/observed?

Locally, VS copies the python scripts to `bin/Debug` (which is `Environment.CurrentDirectory`). When we modify the code at `Algorithm.Python` and build/rebuild, the modified code was not being copied over (I had to manually delete the old file). I tried to modify the properties to "Copy Always" or "Copy if newer", but it just didn't replace the file.
Awesome! Thank you for fixing, I wasn't convinced it was correct before.

Me neither! We could have `_model.GetPythonType().ToString()` instead, but it returns something like `<class 'RsiAlphaModel.RsiAlphaModel'>` and we would have to manipulate this string. Then I look for an alternative and that solution pop out.
Cool! Didn't know `ConvertTo(enumType)` worked like that, awesome!
can python make use of `params` keywords? If not it's OK since *not* having `param` likely reduces the possibility for method ambiguity.

Python can use keyword parameters.  When the keyword is omitted but a value is passed nonetheless, the keyword inherits the positional parameter.  It's bad style to not expressly use named keyword parameters when they exist, because obviously, if the position of the keywords changes with a change to the method definition, then the invoker will no longer function as intended...
@disruptek , `CompositeAlphaModel` is not a python object and we (pythonnet) have an issue on keyword/names parameters. See: https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/issues/1696
I love how simple this has been boiled down to, nice code!
